tfa-cli.label: TODOforAI

tfa-cli.description: Manage the user's OWN TODOforAI tasks (not code `// TODO` comments). Delegate/spin off work: `tfa-cli "prompt"` creates a real TODO with its own agent and chat (`-n` wait for completion, `--no-watch` fire-and-forget, `--project/--agent/--model`, `--resume <id>`, `addmessage <id> "text"`). Inspect: `list [--status open]`, `--inspect <id>`. Edit any todo without opening it: `status <id> DONE|READY|ARCHIVED|POSTPONED|CANCELLED|DELETED` (close, reopen, shelve, trash — `todo restore <id>` undoes a delete) and `todo set <id|-> title=… group=… star=true schedule=<unix-ms> agent=… brand=…` (own todo fields). Both take ONE id, so a loop over `list --json | jq -r '.items[].id'` is how you close, retitle, refile or archive MANY todos at once; `project set|settings|groups …` (name, settings, todo groups), `agent create|update <agent> model=… sysmsg=…` (permissions/MCP/device wiring and delete are refused from an agent shell). Surface results into chat: `show <file|-> [todo-id]` (renders by mimetype, private to the todo's readers; `--card <name>` via project renderer; `--alias <name>` updates in place, `--alias <todoId>:<name>` updates another todo's artifact; `show share <ref>` makes it public and prints the link, `show unshare <ref>` makes it private again), `open <url>` embeds a live preview. Pick by where the output lives: read once → plain reply; interactive, this chat only → `html_snippet`; kept/revised later → `show --alias`, then `show share` only if someone outside needs a link; format the user asked for (pptx, docx…) → `show` the file. Notifications: `inbox [needs-you|messages|activity] [--unread]` reads the user's bell feed (what finished/failed/needs them while away), `inbox seen [tab]` marks it read; `notify "Title" "message" [--href /t/<id>]` leaves a note in the user's Messages tab + phone push (shown as from you); `--to <email>` reaches a member of the current project instead (`project members` lists them, 20/day) — nobody else; same text is delivered once, max 10/day to the user, use for things they must see later (not chat replies). This is the ONLY way to display a local file (image, pdf, html) in the chat: markdown `![](path.png)` with a local/relative path does NOT resolve to workspace files or attachments and 404s in the browser. `--template` for registry workflows.

browser-manager-cli.description: Spawns cloud Chromium sessions, each exposed as a CDP WebSocket for agent-browser to drive. `create` prints one line ending in a cdpUrl — pass it straight to `agent-browser connect '<cdpUrl>'` (connect the cdpUrl, not the Chrome debug port). `list`/`get <id>`, `delete <id>`/`delete-all`, `hibernate`/`restore`. Sessions run stealth Chromium that reads as a real desktop browser. For sites that block datacenter IPs, route through a proxy: `create --proxy socks5://host:port [--proxy-user U --proxy-pass P]`. Use this on the cloud VM instead of launching a local browser.

tfa-explore.label: Explore
tfa-explore.summary: Send a helper agent to explore a codebase and report back.
tfa-explore.description: Sub-agent codebase exploration in its own context, you get only the answer: `tfa-explore "where is auth handled?" [--repo <path>]`. Prefer over manual multi-file searching.

tfa-review.label: Review
tfa-review.summary: Send a helper agent to review your code changes.
tfa-review.description: Sub-agent review of a git diff in its own context: `tfa-review "<goal>" [--repo <path>] [--against <ref>]` (default: uncommitted). Run before calling a non-trivial change done.

tfa-summary.label: Summary
tfa-summary.summary: Summarize files or long output with a helper agent.
tfa-summary.description: Sub-agent summary so raw text never enters your context: `cat big.log | tfa-summary "what failed?"`, or `-f <file>` (repeatable).

tfa-handoff.label: Handoff
tfa-handoff.summary: Turn a long conversation into a short handover note.
tfa-handoff.description: Compact a conversation into a handoff document for a fresh agent.

tfa-wait.label: Wait
tfa-wait.summary: Wait for a time or an event, then continue the task.
tfa-wait.description: Schedule a wake-up: `tfa-wait '<expr>' "<message>"` — expr is a time (`3h`, `daily@9:00`), a webhook, or a command's output; the message arrives later as a new chat message. Wait for a long job: `tfa-wait 'bench || 6h' "Done: exit {{payload.exit}}"` then `tfa-wait run '<cmd>' --pipe bench --on-exit &` (each stdout line = event; cancelling kills the command). Never pgrep/sleep poll loops.

tfa-cloud.label: Cloud SSH
tfa-cloud.summary: SSH host alias for your TODOforAI cloud VM.
tfa-cloud.description: ssh host alias: `ssh tfa-cloud 'command'`, `scp`/`rsync` for files. Same root account, files, tools and logins as the cloud's own bash tool; local and cloud filesystems are separate. Cloud files under `~/.todoforai/mnt/todoforai/`: `todos/"$TODOFORAI_TODO_ID"` (this todo's attachments; double quotes: the id expands locally), `memory/` (your memory of this user). A stopped VM does not wake on connect.

tfa-vault.label: Vault
tfa-vault.description: The user's encrypted secret vault — using its secrets is the intended workflow. READ: when a task needs a key/token/password the user owns, `tfa-vault list` then `get <path>`; don't ask for what's already stored; never echo values. WRITE proactively: any new secret in the conversation (pasted, generated, from a login) → `put <path> field=value` (`patch` adds fields; `put` refuses an existing path — `put --force` replaces all fields on rotation). Paths: `accounts/<svc>`, `api/<svc>`, `secrets/<name>`.

tfa-settings.label: Settings
tfa-settings.summary: Change your TODOforAI app preferences from the shell.
tfa-settings.description: The user's TODOforAI app preferences (AppSettings): `list`, `get <key>`, `set key=value …`, `keys` (documented keys). Use when asked to change theme, list style, tool-block density, thinking traces, sounds/toasts, preview columns, wallpaper etc. Values are JSON when parseable. Consent/credential/escalation keys (shellExecution, notifications, analytics, keyboard bindings, vault provider, billing address) are refused from an agent shell — tell the user to change those in Settings.

tfa-memory.label: Memory
tfa-memory.summary: Your long-term memory of notes, facts and past TODOs.
tfa-memory.description: User's long-term memory (notes/procedures/decisions, address `source/ref`) plus every past TODO message (read-only, `todo/<todoId>:<messageId>`). READ: `search "<topic>" --mode fused` first (`lexical` = all words newest first, `semantic` = meaning; `--source todo` / `--todo <id>` narrow). stderr prints `N row(s) contain a query word` — if N exceeds what you saw, page with `--exclude <address>`. `get <address>` = full row, `around <address> --before N --after N` = surrounding dialogue. Before answering from memory, search once more with your draft's key facts. WRITE durable facts proactively: `add <source>/<ref> "text"` (same address updates in place; short source names like deploy-notes, preferences). `sources` lists them.

todoregistry-cli.label: TODO Registry
todoregistry-cli.description: Reusable business task templates (SEO, email, CRM, ads, social, …): `search <q>`, `get <id>`, `list [category]`, `categories`, `create --name … --description … --body @prompt.md`. To recommend a template, don't create a todo directly — `tfa-cli recommend --template <id> --project <projectId>`.

tfa-surface.label: Surface
tfa-surface.summary: See and control what is on your TODOforAI screen.
tfa-surface.description: The user's live UI from the shell. Everything on screen is a SURFACE holding one ref (a todo id, `<todoId>:<alias>` = a shown artifact, or a url). `describe` lists them (kind, id, ref, focus, embedded-browser CDP URL; `--json`). `open overlay <todoId>` (full page), `open window <ref> [--detached]` (floating; --detached = out of the grid, own size, resizable), `open panel changes|preview|browser|terminal [--url]` (a todo's side panel), `open card <ref> [--title] [--group <slug>]` (a persisted board card every member sees); `close|focus <kind> <id>`. Persistent state (plans, reports, live status) → `show chat.panel <todoId> "...md"` (stdin ok; re-show updates in place), `clear` removes; events go in chat. `card add|list|get|rm <name>` = project HTML renderers. Exit 2 = no frontend connected.

bun.label: JS/TS Runtime
bun.summary: Run JavaScript and TypeScript code, fast.
bun.cloudInstallCmd: export BUN_INSTALL=/usr/local && curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash && ln -sf /usr/local/bin/bun /usr/local/bin/bunx
bun.description: Run JavaScript/TypeScript, install packages, run tests (`bun`, `bunx`).

bunx.summary: Run a JavaScript package without installing it.

npm.label: Node Package Manager
npm.description: Install Node packages and run package scripts.

npx.label: Node Package Runner
npx.summary: Run a JavaScript package without installing it.

uv.label: Python Package Manager
uv.summary: Install Python packages and manage environments, fast.
uv.description: Manage Python dependencies, environments, tools, and scripts (`uv`, `uvx`).

uvx.label: Python Tool Runner
uvx.summary: Run a Python tool without installing it.
uvx.description: Run Python tools in isolated environments.

ripgrep.label: Search
ripgrep.summary: Search text across files, very fast.
ripgrep.description: Fast recursive grep with regex, .gitignore-aware, parallel, unicode-correct

ast-grep.label: Structural Search
ast-grep.summary: Search and rewrite code by its structure, not just text.
ast-grep.description: Use when regex cannot distinguish syntax from text: `ast-grep -p "foo($$$)" -l ts` finds real calls while ignoring strings and comments; add `--rewrite "..."` for codemods. Prefer `rg` for literal or token search.

fd.label: Find Files
fd.summary: Find files and folders by name.

jq.label: JSON
jq.description: Command-line JSON processor: query, filter, transform, format JSON streams

patch.label: Apply Diff

sed.label: Replace Text
sed.summary: Find and replace text in files.
sed.description: Stream editor: in-place text substitution, line filtering, scripted edits

grep.label: Search Text
grep.description: Search plain text for lines matching a regex: recursive, fixed-string, context, invert, count

wordpress-api.label: WordPress
wordpress-api.summary: Read and publish WordPress posts and pages.
wordpress-api.description: WordPress REST API CLI. `wordpress-api auth --site https://example.com --user <user> --password '<application password>'` (application password, not the login password). Reading published content needs no auth. `posts list|get|create|update|delete`, `pages`, `media`, `categories`. `posts create` saves a draft unless --status publish. On Elementor/JetEngine sites content.rendered comes back empty — fetch the post's public URL for the body.

mailchimp-api.label: Mailchimp
mailchimp-api.summary: Manage Mailchimp audiences, contacts, email campaigns and reports.
mailchimp-api.description: Independent CLI over the official Mailchimp Marketing API: 155 endpoint commands for lists (email audiences), members (contacts; email or MD5), tags, segments, merge fields, interests, notes/events, campaigns/content/tests/scheduling, templates, reports, assets, landing pages, classic automations, journey triggers, webhooks and batches. JSON output; --data JSON|@file|-; --schema; --all pagination. Every write requires --yes; use --dry-run first. Raw request METHOD /path covers other Marketing endpoints. API-key auth, not OAuth onboarding. Plan/API restrictions apply; no Transactional/Mandrill or Open Commerce. Run --help for limits and consent cautions.

facebook-pages-api.label: Facebook Pages
facebook-pages-api.summary: Post to your Facebook Page and its linked Instagram account, and handle comments.
facebook-pages-api.description: Facebook Pages CLI (Meta Graph API). `auth --page-id <id> --page-token <token>` (or env FB_PAGE_ID/FB_PAGE_TOKEN). `feed`, `comments`, `insights`, `conversations`, `media`, and `request <GET|POST|DELETE> <path> [--data <json>]` = any Graph edge with the page token attached (use instead of curl). Writes are live: `feed create --published false` for tests; `comments reply` posts publicly — get human approval. Follower totals: `whoami --fields followers_count,fan_count` (many classic insights metrics are retired). Instagram (linked professional account, same page token): `ig whoami|media|get|stories|tags|limit`, `ig publish --image_url U | --video_url U [--media_type STORIES] | --carousel U1,U2 [--caption …]` (public URLs; container → wait → publish; `--create-only` = dry run; 100 posts/24h), `ig comments list|replies|create|reply|hide|delete|toggle`, `ig insights [media_id]` (needs instagram_manage_insights). `--help` for subcommands.

bluesky-api.label: Bluesky
bluesky-api.summary: Post, reply, like and repost on Bluesky, and search or read posts and threads.
bluesky-api.description: Bluesky / AT Protocol XRPC CLI, JSON out. Auth = App Password (Settings → Privacy and security → App passwords), not the main password: `auth --identifier you.bsky.social --password-stdin` (or env BLUESKY_IDENTIFIER/BLUESKY_APP_PASSWORD; `--pds` for self-hosted). Session cached + auto-refreshed — don't re-run auth in loops (createSession 30/5min). Public reads need NO login: `get <post...>`, `thread <post>`, `search <q> [--sort latest --author h --since ISO]`, `feed <actor>`, `profile <actor>`, `followers <actor>`. Login: `timeline`, `post <text> [--reply-to P] [--quote P] [--image f.jpg --alt t]... [--lang en] [--dry-run]` (300 graphemes, links/#tags/@mentions auto-faceted, images ≤1MB ×4), `like <post>`, `repost <post>`, `delete <at-uri>` (post/like/repost). <post> = bsky.app URL or at:// URI. Raw: `api GET|POST <nsid> --param k=v --data JSON` for any lexicon (e.g. app.bsky.notification.listNotifications). Writes are public immediately.

ews-api.label: Exchange (EWS)
ews-api.summary: Read and write mail on a company Exchange server.
ews-api.description: On-prem Microsoft Exchange mail over EWS (cloud/M365 → outlook-api). `auth --email <e> --username 'DOMAIN\\user' --server <host>` (NTLM; password prompt or `--password-stdin`; --server required). Multi-mailbox: `whoami`, `--account <email>`/EWS_ACCOUNT, `default`, `logout`; EWS_EMAIL/EWS_USERNAME/EWS_PASSWORD/EWS_SERVER for unattended runs. `list`, `search <q>`, `read <id>`, `draft`, `reply <id>` — draft/reply stay in Drafts unless --send. Password stored plaintext in ~/.config/ews-api (0600); re-auth after rotation.

outlook-api.label: Outlook (Graph)
outlook-api.summary: Read and write your Outlook mail.
outlook-api.description: Outlook/Hotmail/M365 mail over Microsoft Graph (on-prem Exchange → ews-api). `auth` = device-code flow; `--tenant consumers` (default, personal) | `organizations`. list/search/read/attachments are read-only; `draft`/`reply` stay in Drafts unless --send; `send <draftId>`. `get <path>` = raw Graph GET. JSON out.

neonctl.label: Neon Postgres
neonctl.summary: Manage your Neon Postgres databases and branches.
neonctl.statusCmd: test -f ~/.config/neon/credentials.json && neonctl me --output json 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*"email"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | grep -m10 .
neonctl.description: Manage Neon Postgres branches and run SQL: `neonctl projects list`, `neonctl branches create`, `neonctl connection-string`. Aliased as `neon`.

m365.label: Microsoft 365
m365.summary: Work with Microsoft 365 mail, Teams, SharePoint and users.
m365.statusCmd: m365 status --output text 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | grep -vi 'logged out' | grep -m1 .
m365.description: Microsoft 365 from the shell: `m365 outlook message list`, `m365 teams team list`, `m365 spo site list`. Device-code login; add `--output json` for parseable output.

gws.label: Google Workspace
gws.summary: Work with Google Sheets, Docs, Slides, Drive, Forms, Tasks, Contacts and Chat.
gws.loginTerminalHint: gws needs your own Google OAuth client first: in console.cloud.google.com create a Desktop-app OAuth client (consent screen External/testing, add yourself as test user), enable the APIs you need (Sheets/Docs/Slides/Drive/Forms/Tasks/People/Chat), save the JSON as ~/.config/gws/client_secret.json (or run `gws auth setup` if gcloud is logged in), then `gws auth login -s sheets,drive`.
gws.description: Official Google Workspace CLI, generated from Google's Discovery docs — every Workspace REST method as `gws <service> <resource> <method> --params '<query JSON>' --json '<body JSON>'`; JSON out. `gws schema <service.resource.method>` shows params/body. Sheets: `gws sheets spreadsheets create --json '{"properties":{"title":"T"}}'`, `gws sheets spreadsheets values get --params '{"spreadsheetId":"ID","range":"Sheet1!A1:D10"}'`, `gws sheets spreadsheets values append --params '{"spreadsheetId":"ID","range":"Sheet1","valueInputOption":"USER_ENTERED"}' --json '{"values":[["a",1]]}'`, `values update|clear|batchGet|batchUpdate`, `spreadsheets batchUpdate` (add/delete sheet, formatting); helpers `gws sheets +read` / `+append`. Delete a spreadsheet: `gws drive files delete --params '{"fileId":"ID"}'`. Docs: `gws docs documents create --json '{"title":"T"}'`, `documents get --params '{"documentId":"ID"}'` (text under .body.content), edit via `documents batchUpdate --params '{"documentId":"ID"}' --json '{"requests":[{"insertText":{"location":{"index":1},"text":"hi"}}]}'`. Slides: `gws slides presentations create|get` (presentationId), `presentations batchUpdate` (createSlide, insertText, replaceAllText). Forms: `gws forms forms create --json '{"info":{"title":"T"}}'` (title only; add questions with `forms batchUpdate` createItem), `forms get` (responderUri), `gws forms forms responses list --params '{"formId":"ID"}'`. Tasks: `gws tasks tasklists list|insert|delete`, `gws tasks tasks list|insert|patch|delete --params '{"tasklist":"ID"}'`. Contacts (People API): `gws people people createContact --json '{"names":[{"givenName":"A"}],"emailAddresses":[{"value":"a@x.com"}]}'`, `people get --params '{"resourceName":"people/c…","personFields":"names,emailAddresses"}'`, `people connections list --params '{"resourceName":"people/me","personFields":"names"}'`, `searchContacts` (`readMask`), `deleteContact`. Chat (Workspace accounts only; the OAuth client's GCP project must have a Chat app configured in Console → Chat API → Configuration, else 404 "Chat app not found"): `gws chat spaces list`, `spaces create --json '{"spaceType":"SPACE","displayName":"N"}'`, `gws chat spaces messages create --params '{"parent":"spaces/ID"}' --json '{"text":"hi"}'`, `messages list`, `spaces delete` (needs chat.delete scope). Docs/Slides/Forms files are deleted with `gws drive files delete`. `--page-all` paginates, `--dry-run` validates. Auth precedence: env GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_CLI_TOKEN (access token) > GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_CLI_CREDENTIALS_FILE (service-account or exported authorized_user JSON) > `gws auth login`. A 403 "API has not been used in project N" means enable that API in the OAuth client's GCP project; a 403 "insufficient authentication scopes" right after re-login with more scopes → delete ~/.config/gws/token_cache.json (stale access token).

hubspot.label: HubSpot
hubspot.summary: Work with your HubSpot contacts, deals and content.
hubspot.description: Invoked as `hs`. `hs api <endpoint>` makes authenticated calls to any HubSpot API (contacts, deals, companies) — prefer it over raw curl.

posthog-cli.label: PostHog
posthog-cli.summary: Query PostHog product analytics and manage feature flags.
posthog-cli.loginTerminalHint: Interactive only: run `posthog-cli login` in a terminal on this host (it asks for host, project and a personal API key), or set `POSTHOG_CLI_API_KEY` + `POSTHOG_CLI_PROJECT_ID`.
posthog-cli.description: Official PostHog CLI. `posthog-cli api tools` lists the agent-first API tool catalog, `posthog-cli api call <tool> '<json>'` runs one (SQL queries, insights, flags). Also uploads sourcemaps/dSYM. Env alternative: POSTHOG_CLI_API_KEY + POSTHOG_CLI_PROJECT_ID.

canva.label: Canva
canva.description: Official Canva CLI — app-development focused: `canva apps create/list/preview`. `canva mcp` starts the Canva Developer MCP server. For design/export automation use the Canva Connect REST API.

webflow.label: Webflow
webflow.summary: Manage Webflow sites, CMS content and assets.
webflow.description: Manage Webflow sites from the shell: `webflow sites list`, `webflow cms ...`, `webflow assets ...`. Add `--skip-update-check` in scripts.

readwise.label: Readwise
readwise.summary: Search and save articles and highlights in Readwise.
readwise.statusCmd: readwise whoami >/dev/null 2>&1 && readwise whoami 2>/dev/null | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | grep -m1 .
readwise.description: Official Readwise/Reader CLI. `readwise search <query>`, `readwise list`, `readwise save <url>`; supports JSON output for piping and a read-only mode for agents. Token login for CI: `readwise login-with-token <token>` (get one at readwise.io/access_token).

granola.label: Granola
granola.summary: Read your Granola meeting notes and transcripts.
granola.statusCmd: granola auth status -o json 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*"authenticated": *true.*/authenticated/p' | grep -m1 .
granola.loginTerminalHint: Imports the Granola desktop app's session: install Granola on this host, sign in there, then run `granola auth login`.
granola.description: Community Granola CLI (read-only). `granola meeting list [-l N] [--since <date>] [-s <query>] [-a <attendee>] -o json`, `granola meeting notes|enhanced|transcript <id>`, `granola meeting export <id>`; `granola folder list`, `granola workspace list`. `-o json|yaml|toon` for piping. Login imports credentials from the installed Granola desktop app (`granola auth login`) — desktop app must be logged in on the same machine; transcripts need a paid Granola plan.

trello.label: Trello
trello.summary: Manage your Trello boards, lists and cards.
trello.description: Community Trello CLI (mheap/trello-cli, no official one exists). Auth is a Trello API key + token from https://trello.com/app-key — `trello auth:api-key <key>` then `trello auth:token <token>`. `board:list`, `list:list --board <name>`, `card:list --board <b> --list <l>`, `card:create --board <b> --list <l> --name <n> [--description ..] [--due <date>]`, `card:move`, `card:comment`, `label:*`, `search <q>`. Add `--format json` for piping. Names resolve via a local cache; run `trello board:list` once after login to warm it.

mapps.label: monday.com
mapps.description: Invoked as `mapps` — app development and monday-code deployments only; `mapps init -t <token>` stores a monday.com API token in ~/.mappsrc. To read/write board DATA use the monday.com GraphQL API (api.monday.com/v2) with that same token.

exa-cli.label: Exa Search
exa-cli.summary: Search the web and pull page contents, built for AI.
exa-cli.description: Invoked as `exa`. `exa search <query>`, `exa answer <question>`, `exa contents <url>`, `exa find-similar <url>` — JSON by default. Needs EXA_API_KEY in the environment (get one at dashboard.exa.ai); store it in the vault.

mobbin.label: Mobbin
mobbin.summary: Browse real app and website design examples.
mobbin.statusCmd: mobbin auth print-cookie 2>/dev/null | grep -E '[A-Za-z0-9]' >/dev/null && echo authenticated
mobbin.loginTerminalHint: Log in to mobbin.com in a browser on this host, then run `mobbin auth save-cookie`: it imports that browser's cookies.
mobbin.description: Unofficial CLI over Mobbin's undocumented web endpoints. `mobbin search --query "login" --platform ios`. Auth reuses browser cookies: log into mobbin.com in Chrome, then `mobbin auth save-cookie`.

blender-mcp.label: Blender
blender-mcp.summary: Model, texture and render 3D scenes in a running Blender.
blender-mcp.statusCmd: command -v blender-mcp >/dev/null && mcporter call blender.get_addon_status --output json 2>/dev/null | grep -o '"blender_version": "[^"]*"' | grep -m1 .
blender-mcp.loginTerminalHint: Needs Blender (blender.org) open on this host: in Blender, Edit → Preferences → Add-ons, enable `Blender MCP`, then press N in the 3D view → BlenderMCP tab → Connect / Start MCP server. Then press Connect here.
blender-mcp.loginCmd: blender-mcp install-addon >/dev/null 2>&1; command -v mcporter >/dev/null 2>&1 || npm install -g --prefix "$HOME/.local" mcporter; mcporter config add blender --command blender-mcp --env BLENDER_MCP_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 --description 'Blender 3D via ahujasid/blender-mcp addon' --scope home
blender-mcp.description: Blender 3D via the ahujasid/blender-mcp server through mcporter: `mcporter list blender --schema`, `mcporter call blender.<tool> key=value` (`code=@file.py`; every tool needs `user_prompt`). Workhorse: execute_blender_code (any bpy Python); also scene/object info, viewport screenshot (`--save-images <dir>`), PolyHaven/Sketchfab import. Needs a GUI Blender with the addon server started (socket :9876; headless has none). 'Could not connect' → `blender-mcp install-addon`, enable in Preferences → Add-ons, N-panel → Start MCP Server (scripted: `blender --python s.py`, s.py registers a `bpy.app.timers` calling `bpy.ops.blendermcp.start_server()`). Code runs unguarded: save first (`bpy.ops.wm.save_mainfile()`), approve destructive ops.
blender-mcp.versionCmd: { python -c 'import sys; from importlib.metadata import version; print(version(sys.argv[1]))' blender-mcp || python3 -c 'import sys; from importlib.metadata import version; print(version(sys.argv[1]))' blender-mcp; } 2>/dev/null

google-ads.label: Google Ads
google-ads.summary: Query and manage Google Ads campaigns, keywords and conversions.
google-ads.loginCmd:
printf 'developer_token: %s
client_id: %s
client_secret: %s
refresh_token: %s
login_customer_id: %s
use_proto_plus: true
' <developer_token> <client_id> <client_secret> <refresh_token> <mcc_id_digits_only> > "$HOME/google-ads.yaml" && python3 -c 'from google.ads.googleads.client import GoogleAdsClient; GoogleAdsClient.load_from_storage(); print("ok")'
google-ads.statusCmd: python3 -c 'from google.ads.googleads.client import GoogleAdsClient; c=GoogleAdsClient.load_from_storage(); print(c.login_customer_id or "authenticated")' 2>/dev/null | grep -m1 .
google-ads.versionCmd: python -c 'import google.ads.googleads as g; print(g.VERSION)' 2>/dev/null || python3 -c 'import google.ads.googleads as g; print(g.VERSION)' 2>/dev/null
google-ads.description: Official Google Ads API client library (Python) — there is no official CLI, so call it via `python3 -c` or a script. Config `~/google-ads.yaml` (developer_token, client_id/secret, refresh_token, login_customer_id = MCC digits). Mint refresh_token with the bundled `google-oauthlib-tool --client-secrets <json> --scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/adwords --save --headless` (or examples/authentication/generate_user_credentials.py). Read: `client.get_service('GoogleAdsService').search_stream(customer_id=<digits>, query=<GAQL>)`. Write: `<X>Service.mutate_<x>s(customer_id, operations, validate_only=True)` first, then real. Keyword ideas: `KeywordPlanIdeaService.generate_keyword_ideas`. Offline conversions: `ConversionUploadService.upload_click_conversions`. Customer ids are digits without dashes.

cua-driver.label: Desktop Control
cua-driver.summary: Click, type and read native desktop apps without taking over the mouse or focus.

cua-driver.description: Native desktop automation (macOS/Windows/Linux X11; Wayland only via AT-SPI, no window screenshots) through the accessibility tree — actions land in the BACKGROUND without moving the user's focus or pointer. Needs a daemon: `cua-driver status || (cua-driver serve --no-overlay >/dev/null 2>&1 &)`; on macOS grant permissions first with `cua-driver permissions grant`; on Windows the daemon must run in the interactive desktop session (`cua-driver autostart enable` registers a logon task). Loop: `cua-driver call list_windows '{}'` → pid+window_id; `cua-driver call get_window_state '{"pid":P,"window_id":W,"include_screenshot":false}'` → `elements[]` with `element_token`; act with `cua-driver call click '{"pid":P,"window_id":W,"element_token":"s..:N"}'`, `type_text {..,"text":".."}`, `hotkey {..,"keys":["ctrl","s"]}`, `press_key`, `scroll`, `invoke_menu`. Tokens are snapshot-bound: re-run get_window_state after EVERY action (stale token = refusal). Window screenshot: add `--screenshot-out-file out.png` (`max_dimension` to shrink). Responses say `effect:unverifiable` — verify from a fresh tree, not from the click reply. `delivery_mode:"foreground"` steals focus; use only when asked. Chrome/Electron trees are near-empty — use agent-browser for web pages. `cua-driver list-tools` / `describe <tool>` for the full surface; `cua-driver mcp` exposes the same over stdio MCP.

apollo.label: Apollo.io
apollo.summary: Find and enrich B2B leads and manage Apollo contacts, deals and sequences.
apollo.loginCmd: mcporter config add apollo --url https://mcp.apollo.io/mcp --header X-Api-Key=<master_api_key> --description 'Apollo.io (official MCP)' --scope home
apollo.statusCmd: mcporter call apollo.apollo_users_api_profile --output json 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*"email": *"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | grep -m1 .
apollo.description: Apollo.io through its official MCP server (mcporter server `apollo`, 85 tools, all plans incl. free). Key: https://developer.apollo.io/#/keys → Create new key → toggle 'Set as master key' (the MCP rejects scoped keys). `mcporter list apollo` shows every tool with its args. Prospecting: `mcporter call apollo.apollo_mixed_people_api_search --args '{"q_organization_domains_list":["acme.com"],"person_titles":["cto"],"per_page":10}'` (no credits, emails hidden), `apollo_people_match` (email/name+domain → enriched person, costs credits), `apollo_organizations_enrich domain=acme.com`, `apollo_mixed_companies_search`, `apollo_organizations_job_postings`. CRM: apollo_contacts_create/update/search, apollo_accounts_*, apollo_deals_*; sequences: apollo_emailer_campaigns_search, apollo_emailer_campaigns_add_contact_ids. Credits balance: apollo_users_api_profile. REST fallback: curl https://api.apollo.io/api/v1/... -H 'x-api-key: <key>' (docs https://docs.apollo.io/reference).

lusha.label: Lusha
lusha.summary: Find and enrich B2B contacts and companies with Lusha data.
lusha.loginCmd: mcporter config add lusha --url https://mcp.lusha.com --header x-api-key=<api_key> --description 'Lusha (official MCP)' --scope home
lusha.statusCmd: mcporter call lusha.account_usage reason_for_invocation=status --output json 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*"remaining": *\([0-9]*\).*/\1 credits left/p' | grep -m1 .
lusha.description: Lusha through its official MCP server (mcporter server `lusha`, 48 tools; free plan: 40 credits/mo, 100 req/day). Key: dashboard.lusha.com → API & connectors → Copy API key (sent as `x-api-key`, no Bearer). Every tool needs `reason_for_invocation`. Prospecting is free, reveals cost credits: `mcporter call lusha.prospecting_contact_search --args '{"reason_for_invocation":"find CTOs","jobTitles":["CTO"],...}'` → ids → `prospecting_contact_enrich` (ids, reveal:["emails","phones"]); `prospecting_company_search domains:[…]`/`prospecting_company_enrich`; `contacts_search`/`companies_search` for direct name+company/LinkedIn/email lookup; `lookalike_contacts`/`lookalike_companies`; filter vocabularies via `prospecting_contact_filters`/`prospecting_company_filters type=…`; `account_usage` shows credits. `mcporter list lusha` for all args. Docs: https://docs.lusha.com/mcp/overview

todoist.label: Todoist
todoist.summary: Add, find and complete your Todoist tasks and projects.
todoist.description: Official Todoist CLI (Doist), invoked as `td`. Always pass `--json` (or `--ndjson`) for parseable output. Tasks: `td task add "<content>" [--due tomorrow] [--priority p1] [--project <name|id:x>] [--section ..] [--labels a,b] [--description ..] --json`, `td task qa "Buy milk tomorrow p1 #Shopping"` (natural-language quick add), `td task list [--project ..] [--filter '<todoist filter>'] [--due today|overdue] --json`, `td task view|complete|uncomplete|update|move|reschedule|delete <ref>` (ref = name or `id:xxx`). Shortcuts: `td today`, `td upcoming`, `td inbox`, `td completed`. Also `td project|section|label|comment|reminder|filter|workspace ... --json`, `td view <todoist URL>`. Writes support `--dry-run`. Auth: API token from Todoist Settings → Integrations → Developer, `td auth token <token> --credential-store=plaintext` (headless hosts have no keyring; default `system` store fails there), or env `TODOIST_API_TOKEN` (wins over stored). `td auth status --json` shows the account. Docs: https://developer.todoist.com/api/v1/ (old REST v2 is gone: HTTP 410).

calcom.label: Cal.com
calcom.summary: See your Cal.com bookings and free slots, and book, reschedule or cancel meetings.
calcom.description: Official Cal.com CLI over API v2 (calcom/companion). Add `--json` to every command (default output is a table). `calcom me show --json`; `calcom event-types list|get|create|update|delete`; `calcom slots available --event-type-id <id> --start 2026-10-07 --end 2026-10-08 [--timezone Europe/Budapest] --json` (free slots; or `--event-type-slug <slug> --username <user>`); `calcom bookings list|get <uid>|create --event-type-id <id> --start <ISO UTC> --attendee-name .. --attendee-email .. --attendee-timezone ..|cancel <uid>|reschedule <uid>|confirm|decline|mark-no-show|add-guests`; `calcom agenda` (upcoming); also schedules, calendars, webhooks, ooo, teams/org-*. Auth: API key from Settings → Developer → API keys (`cal_live_…`, free plan) — `calcom login --api-key <key>` or env `CAL_API_KEY` (+ `CAL_API_URL` for self-hosted). Docs: https://cal.com/docs/api-reference/v2/introduction

toggltrack-api.label: Toggl Track
toggltrack-api.summary: Track time in Toggl Track: timers, time entries, projects, clients, tasks and tags.
toggltrack-api.description: Independent CLI over the Toggl Track API v9 (raw 1:1 fields, JSON out). Token: https://track.toggl.com/profile → API Token (or TOGGL_API_TOKEN); Toggl 2.0 `toggl_sk_` keys do not work here. Workspace-scoped commands use the default workspace saved at auth, or -w <id> / TOGGL_WORKSPACE_ID (`me workspaces` lists them). Timers: `toggltrack-api entries start --data '{"description":"Call","project_id":123,"tags":["client"]}'`, `entries current`, `entries stop <id>`; finished entry: `entries create --data '{"start":"2026-10-05T09:00:00Z","duration":3600,"description":"…"}'`; `entries list --query start_date=2026-10-01 --query end_date=2026-10-06`. Also clients, projects, tasks (paid plans), tags, users: list/get/create/update/delete. Anything else: `toggltrack-api api <METHOD> /<path>` (relative to /api/v9). DELETE needs --yes; --dry-run previews. Docs: https://engineering.toggl.com/docs/track/

calendly-api.label: Calendly
calendly-api.summary: Find Calendly events and invitees, create booking links, cancel events.
calendly-api.description: Independent CLI over the Calendly API v2 (raw 1:1 fields, JSON out). Token: https://calendly.com/integrations/api_webhooks → Personal access tokens (scopes Scheduling, User management, Webhooks) or CALENDLY_TOKEN. IDs take a uuid or full URI; list commands default to the authenticated user. Find an invitee: `calendly-api events list --query invitee_email=a@acme.com --query status=active`, then `invitees list <event_uuid>`. Single-use link: `calendly-api links create --data '{"owner":"<event_type uri from event-types list>"}'` → booking_url. One-off meeting: `event-types one-off --data '{"name":"Intro","duration":30,"date_setting":{"type":"date_range","start_date":"…","end_date":"…"},"location":{"kind":"custom","location":"Zoom"}}'`. Cancel (notifies invitees): `events cancel <uuid> --data '{"reason":"…"}' --yes`. Also members, event-types available-times, no-shows, availability busy-times, webhooks (paid). Anything else: `calendly-api api <METHOD> /<path>`. Docs: https://developer.calendly.com/llms.txt

clickup-api.label: ClickUp
clickup-api.summary: Manage ClickUp tasks, lists, comments, checklists, goals and time tracking.
clickup-api.description: Independent CLI over the ClickUp API v2 (raw 1:1 fields, JSON out). Token: ClickUp → Settings → ClickUp API → API tokens (pk_…) or CLICKUP_API_TOKEN; OAuth tokens work too. Hierarchy workspace(team) → spaces → folders → lists → tasks; workspace-scoped commands use the saved workspace or -t <team_id>. Find: `clickup-api spaces list`, `lists folderless <space_id>` / `lists list <folder_id>`, `tasks list <list_id> --query statuses[]=open`, `tasks search --query assignees[]=<user_id>`. Write: `tasks create <list_id> --data '{"name":"…","assignees":[123],"due_date":<ms>,"priority":2}'`, `tasks update <id> --data '{"status":"in progress"}'`, `comments create <task_id> --data '{"comment_text":"…"}'`, `checklists create <task_id>`, `tasks set-field <task_id> <field_id> --data '{"value":…}'`. Time: `time start --data '{"tid":"<task_id>"}'`, `time current`, `time stop`, `time list --query start_date=<ms>`. Also folders, goals/key-results, tags, time-tags, webhooks. Timestamps in ms. Anything else: `clickup-api api <METHOD> /<path>` (relative to /api/v2). DELETE needs --yes; --dry-run previews. Docs: https://developer.clickup.com/llms.txt

meistertask.label: MeisterTask
meistertask.summary: Create and update MeisterTask tasks, labels, checklists and attachments.
meistertask.loginCmd: command -v mcporter >/dev/null 2>&1 || npm install -g --prefix "$HOME/.local" mcporter; cd ~ && mcporter config add meistertask --url https://mcp.meistertask.com/mcp --header 'Authorization=Bearer <personal_access_token>' --description 'MeisterTask (official MCP)' --scope home
meistertask.statusCmd: mcporter call meistertask.mt_whoami --output json 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^  "firstname"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1 (MeisterTask)/p' | grep -m1 .
meistertask.description: MeisterTask's official remote MCP (https://mcp.meistertask.com/mcp) through mcporter, authenticated with a personal access token: https://www.mindmeister.com/api → Personal access tokens → Add, scopes userinfo.email userinfo.profile meistertask (MeisterTask accounts reach it via accounts.meister.co; enable the free MindMeister product first if the page redirects to Plans). `mcporter list meistertask --schema` for all ~40 tools; `mcporter call meistertask.<tool> key=value`. Chain: `mt_projects_list` → `mt_sections_list projectId=…` → `mt_tasks_create sectionId=… name=… notes=… assignedToId=… due=<iso>`; `mt_tasks_update id=… status=completed`, `mt_tasks_search text=… status='["open"]'`, `mt_labels_list|create projectId=… name=… color=<hex>`, `mt_tasks_labels_add taskId=… labelId=…`, `mt_tasks_attachments_create_external taskId=… url=…` / `mt_tasks_attachments_upload`, `mt_checklists_create`, `mt_tasks_comments_create`, `mt_persons_list` (people), `mt_whoami`. Lists come back as compact TOON text; single objects as JSON. Raw REST (same token, Bearer): https://www.meistertask.com/api/<resource>, docs https://developers.meistertask.com/llms.txt.

zoomadmin-api.label: Zoom
zoomadmin-api.summary: Manage Zoom meetings, webinars, registrants, cloud recordings and users.
zoomadmin-api.description: Independent CLI over the Zoom REST API v2 (raw 1:1 fields, JSON out). Auth: a Server-to-Server OAuth app (marketplace.zoom.us → Develop → Build app → Server to Server OAuth; add meeting/webinar/cloud_recording/user :admin scopes; Activate) → account_id + client_id + client_secret, or env ZOOM_ACCOUNT_ID/ZOOM_CLIENT_ID/ZOOM_CLIENT_SECRET; ZOOM_ACCESS_TOKEN accepts any ready OAuth token. User-scoped commands take -u <id|email> (default me). Meetings: `meetings list`, `meetings create --data '{"topic":"…","type":2,"start_time":"2026-10-20T10:00:00Z","duration":30}'`, `meetings get|update|delete|end <id>`, `meetings participants <id>`. Registrants: `meeting-registrants add <id> --data '{"email":"…","first_name":"…"}'`, `webinar-registrants list|add|status <webinarId>`. Webinars: `webinars list|create`, `webinars get|update|delete <id>`, `panelists list|add|delete`. Recordings: `recordings list --query from=YYYY-MM-DD`, `recordings get|delete <meetingId>`, `recordings transcript <meetingId>`. `users list|get`, `call-logs list` (Zoom Phone). Registrants/participants need a paid plan, webinars the Webinar add-on. Anything else: `zoomadmin-api api <METHOD> /<path>` (relative to /v2). DELETE needs --yes; --dry-run previews. Docs: https://developers.zoom.us/docs/api/

postmark-mcp.label: Postmark
postmark-mcp.summary: Send transactional email with Postmark and check bounces and delivery stats.
postmark-mcp.loginCmd: command -v mcporter >/dev/null 2>&1 || npm install -g --prefix "$HOME/.local" mcporter; cd ~ && mcporter config add postmark --command postmark-mcp --env POSTMARK_SERVER_TOKEN=<server_token> --env DEFAULT_SENDER_EMAIL=<sender_email> --env DEFAULT_MESSAGE_STREAM=outbound --description 'Postmark transactional email (official MCP)' --scope home
postmark-mcp.statusCmd: command -v postmark-mcp >/dev/null && mcporter call postmark.getServerInfo --output json 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*"Server: \([^\\]*\).*/\1/p' | grep -m1 .
postmark-mcp.description: Postmark's official MCP (@activecampaign/postmark-mcp, stdio) via mcporter server `postmark`: `mcporter call postmark.<tool> key=value --output json`, schemas `mcporter list postmark --schema`. Tools: sendEmail (to, subject, textBody/htmlBody, from defaults to the sender given at login), sendEmailWithTemplate (templateId|templateAlias + templateModel), sendBatch/sendBatchWithTemplate, listTemplates/getTemplate/createTemplate/editTemplate/deleteTemplate/validateTemplate, searchOutboundMessages/getMessageDetails/diagnoseDelivery, searchBounces/getBounceDump/activateBounce, listSuppressions/createSuppressions/deleteSuppressions, getDeliveryStats, getServerInfo, listWebhooks/createWebhook/deleteWebhook. Server token: account.postmarkapp.com → Servers → API Tokens; the sender must be a confirmed Sender Signature. New accounts are in Test mode until Postmark approves them (only same-domain recipients). Other stream: re-run login with DEFAULT_MESSAGE_STREAM=<id>. Never install the unscoped `postmark-mcp` npm package (malicious, removed). REST: https://postmarkapp.com/developer (header X-Postmark-Server-Token).

mailgun-mcp.label: Mailgun
mailgun-mcp.summary: Send email with Mailgun and manage domains, mailing lists, events and stats.
mailgun-mcp.loginCmd: command -v mcporter >/dev/null 2>&1 || npm install -g --prefix "$HOME/.local" mcporter; cd ~ && mcporter config add mailgun --command mailgun-mcp-server --env MAILGUN_API_KEY=<api_key> --description 'Mailgun email API (official MCP)' --scope home
mailgun-mcp.statusCmd: command -v mailgun-mcp-server >/dev/null && mcporter call mailgun.get-v4-domains --output json 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*completed successfully.*/authenticated/p' | grep -m1 .
mailgun-mcp.description: Mailgun's official MCP (@mailgun/mcp-server, stdio) via mcporter server `mailgun`: `mcporter call mailgun.<tool> key=value --output json`, schemas `mcporter list mailgun --schema`. Tools are named after the REST route: post-v3-domain-messages (send: `--args '{"domain_name":"…","from":"…","to":["…"],"subject":"…","text":"…"}'`; `to` is an array), get-v4-domains, get-v3-lists / post-v3-lists-list_address-members (mailing list members), get-v3-domain-bounces/unsubscribes/complaints, get-v3-domain-templates, get-v3-routes, get-v3-stats-total, post-v1-analytics-logs (events), validate_email, get_metrics_summary. API key: app.mailgun.com → API Security. EU accounts: re-run login adding `--env MAILGUN_API_REGION=eu`. Free accounts send only from the sandbox domain to authorized recipients, and sending stays disabled until the account is activated (phone). REST docs: https://documentation.mailgun.com (Basic auth api:<key>).

brevo.label: Brevo
brevo.summary: Manage Brevo contacts, email and SMS campaigns, transactional email and CRM.
brevo.statusCmd: mcporter list https://mcp.brevo.com/v1/brevo/mcp --name brevo --status --exit-code 2>/dev/null | grep -o '[0-9]* tools' | grep -m1 .
brevo.logoutCmd: cd ~ && mcporter config add brevo https://mcp.brevo.com/v1/brevo/mcp --scope home >/dev/null && mcporter config logout brevo && mcporter config remove brevo
brevo.description: Brevo's official MCP (https://mcp.brevo.com/v1/brevo/mcp) via mcporter, OAuth login (works without an API key, which Brevo gates behind phone verification). Call: `mcporter call --http-url https://mcp.brevo.com/v1/brevo/mcp --name brevo <tool> key=value --output json`; schemas: `mcporter list https://mcp.brevo.com/v1/brevo/mcp --name brevo --schema`. ~280 tools prefixed by module: contacts_*/lists_*/attributes_* (contacts, lists, attributes), email_campaign_*/sms_*/whatsapp_* (campaigns), transac_* (send transactional email, templates, logs), templates_*, senders_*/domains_*, deals_*/companies_*/tasks_*/notes_* (CRM), ecommerce_*/loyalty_*/coupons_*, webhooks_*, accounts_get_account (plan, credits). Free plan: 300 emails/day. REST alternative: https://developers.brevo.com (header api-key).

maileroo.label: Maileroo
maileroo.summary: Send transactional email with Maileroo and verify email addresses.
maileroo.statusCmd: mcporter list https://api.maileroo.com/mcp --name maileroo --status --exit-code 2>/dev/null | grep -o '[0-9]* tools' | grep -m1 .
maileroo.logoutCmd: cd ~ && mcporter config add maileroo https://api.maileroo.com/mcp --scope home >/dev/null && mcporter config logout maileroo && mcporter config remove maileroo
maileroo.description: Maileroo's official MCP (https://api.maileroo.com/mcp) via mcporter, OAuth login (the MCP refuses API keys). Call: `mcporter call --http-url https://api.maileroo.com/mcp --name maileroo <tool> key=value --output json`; schemas: `mcporter list https://api.maileroo.com/mcp --name maileroo --schema`. Tools cover sending email (plain or template), sending domains, email verification and account management. REST alternative: https://maileroo.com/docs (header X-API-Key, base https://smtp.maileroo.com/api/v2).

kit.label: Kit
kit.summary: Manage Kit (ConvertKit) subscribers, tags, sequences, broadcasts and forms.
kit.statusCmd: mcporter list https://app.kit.com/mcp --name kit --status --exit-code 2>/dev/null | grep -o '[0-9]* tools' | grep -m1 .
kit.logoutCmd: cd ~ && mcporter config add kit https://app.kit.com/mcp --scope home >/dev/null && mcporter config logout kit && mcporter config remove kit
kit.description: Kit's official MCP (https://app.kit.com/mcp) via mcporter, OAuth login. Call: `mcporter call --http-url https://app.kit.com/mcp --name kit <tool> key=value --output json`; schemas: `mcporter list https://app.kit.com/mcp --name kit --schema`. Tools cover subscribers (list, create, update), tags, custom fields, segments, sequences, broadcasts (draft and stats), forms, purchases and webhooks. REST alternative: https://developers.kit.com (v4, header X-Kit-Api-Key).

klaviyo.label: Klaviyo
klaviyo.summary: Manage Klaviyo profiles, lists, segments, campaigns, flows and reports.
klaviyo.statusCmd: mcporter list https://mcp.klaviyo.com/mcp --name klaviyo --status --exit-code 2>/dev/null | grep -o '[0-9]* tools' | grep -m1 .
klaviyo.logoutCmd: cd ~ && mcporter config add klaviyo https://mcp.klaviyo.com/mcp --scope home >/dev/null && mcporter config logout klaviyo && mcporter config remove klaviyo
klaviyo.description: Klaviyo's official remote MCP (https://mcp.klaviyo.com/mcp) via mcporter, OAuth login (Owner, Admin or Manager role). Call: `mcporter call --http-url https://mcp.klaviyo.com/mcp --name klaviyo <tool> key=value --output json`; schemas: `mcporter list https://mcp.klaviyo.com/mcp --name klaviyo --schema`. Tools cover campaigns, flows, profiles, lists and segments, reporting, catalogs, events, forms, templates, webhooks, coupons, tags and reviews; writes are separate tools from reads. Private-key alternative: REST https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/reference/api_overview (header `Authorization: Klaviyo-API-Key pk_…`, `revision` header required).

sendpulse.label: SendPulse
sendpulse.summary: Run SendPulse email campaigns, manage mailing lists and read campaign stats.
sendpulse.statusCmd: mcporter list https://mcp.sendpulse.com/mcp --name sendpulse --status --exit-code 2>/dev/null | grep -o '[0-9]* tools' | grep -m1 .
sendpulse.logoutCmd: cd ~ && mcporter config add sendpulse https://mcp.sendpulse.com/mcp --scope home >/dev/null && mcporter config logout sendpulse && mcporter config remove sendpulse
sendpulse.description: SendPulse's official MCP (https://mcp.sendpulse.com/mcp) via mcporter, OAuth login. Call: `mcporter call --http-url https://mcp.sendpulse.com/mcp --name sendpulse <tool> key=value --output json`; schemas: `mcporter list https://mcp.sendpulse.com/mcp --name sendpulse --schema`. Tools cover mailing lists and contacts, email campaigns and their statistics, and account info. Headless alternative: API ID and secret from Account settings → API as `--header X-SP-ID=<id> --header X-SP-SECRET=<secret>`. REST: https://sendpulse.com/integrations/api.

beehiiv.label: beehiiv
beehiiv.summary: Draft beehiiv newsletter posts and manage subscribers, segments and automations.
beehiiv.statusCmd: mcporter list https://mcp.beehiiv.com/mcp --name beehiiv --status --exit-code 2>/dev/null | grep -o '[0-9]* tools' | grep -m1 .
beehiiv.logoutCmd: cd ~ && mcporter config add beehiiv https://mcp.beehiiv.com/mcp --scope home >/dev/null && mcporter config logout beehiiv && mcporter config remove beehiiv
beehiiv.description: beehiiv's official MCP (https://mcp.beehiiv.com/mcp) via mcporter, OAuth login. Call: `mcporter call --http-url https://mcp.beehiiv.com/mcp --name beehiiv <tool> key=value --output json`; schemas: `mcporter list https://mcp.beehiiv.com/mcp --name beehiiv --schema`. Tools: post drafts, templates and tags; subscribers, segments, custom fields, surveys and polls; signup forms and recommendations; paywalls, tiers and ads; automations; podcasts; website SEO and redirects. Publishing or scheduling posts and activating automations are not exposed. Free plan is read-only; paid plans can write. Several publications: append `?account=<id>` to the URL. REST alternative: https://developers.beehiiv.com (Bearer API key, paid plans).

freshdesk-api.label: Freshdesk
freshdesk-api.summary: Manage Freshdesk tickets, replies, notes, contacts, companies and agents.
freshdesk-api.description: Independent CLI over the Freshdesk REST API v2 (https://<domain>.freshdesk.com/api/v2), JSON out. Auth = API key (Profile settings → View API key) + helpdesk domain: `auth --domain acme --key-stdin` (or env FRESHDESK_API_KEY/FRESHDESK_DOMAIN). Commands for tickets (list/get/create/update/delete/restore, reply, note, conversations, forward, bulk-update, fields), contacts, companies, agents, groups, canned responses, solutions and search (`search tickets --query '"status:2"'`); --all pagination; raw `api METHOD /path`. Every write requires --yes; use --dry-run first. Plan limits apply (rate limits per plan; the free plan is discontinued, trial keys expire).

chatwoot-api.label: Chatwoot
chatwoot-api.summary: Manage Chatwoot conversations, messages, contacts, inboxes and agents.
chatwoot-api.description: Independent CLI over the Chatwoot Application API, generated from the official swagger (124 endpoints): conversations (list/filter/assign/toggle status/labels), messages, contacts, inboxes, agents, teams, canned responses, labels, custom attributes, webhooks, automation rules, reports. JSON out; --data JSON|@file|-; --all pagination; raw `api METHOD /path`. Auth = user access token (Profile settings → Access token): `auth --token-stdin [--base-url https://chat.example.com] [--account-id N]` (or env CHATWOOT_API_ACCESS_TOKEN/CHATWOOT_BASE_URL/CHATWOOT_ACCOUNT_ID); default base https://app.chatwoot.com, self-hosted supported. On Chatwoot Cloud the user API token needs a paid plan; agent-bot tokens only reach conversation/message endpoints. Every write requires --yes; use --dry-run first.

discord-api.label: Discord
discord-api.summary: Send Discord messages and manage channels, servers, members, roles and webhooks.
discord-api.description: Independent CLI over the Discord REST API v10, generated from the official OpenAPI spec (246 operations): channels/messages/reactions/threads, guilds (servers), members, roles, bans, invites, webhooks, application commands, users/DMs. JSON out; --data JSON|@file|-; --all snowflake pagination; raw `api METHOD /path`. Auth = bot token (Developer Portal → Bot → Reset Token): `auth --token-stdin` (or env DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN; `--bearer` / DISCORD_ACCESS_TOKEN for an OAuth2 user token). A bot only sees servers it was added to (authorize URL with scope=bot, opened by a server admin). Webhook token routes need no login. Every write requires --yes; use --dry-run first. REST only (no gateway events); no multipart uploads.

twitch-api.label: Twitch
twitch-api.summary: Manage Twitch channels, followers, clips, streams, chat and moderation.
twitch-api.statusCmd: twitch-api whoami 2>/dev/null | sed -n -e 's/.*"login"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/1 \1/p' -e 's/.*"client_id"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/2 app:\1/p' | sort | cut -d' ' -f2 | grep -m1 .
twitch-api.description: Independent CLI over the Twitch Helix API, generated from the official reference (149 endpoints): channels (info/modify/followers/editors), users (lookup/block), clips, streams, videos, games, search, chat (send/settings/emotes), moderation (bans/mods/VIPs), subscriptions, polls/predictions, schedule, raids, EventSub subscriptions.
